title: I–V line of a 15 Ω resistor
caption: A resistor with 4.5 V across it and 0.3 A through it has R = V/I = 15 Ω. Its I–V line is straight through the origin, with gradient 1/R = 0.067 A V⁻¹: doubling the voltage to 9 V doubles the current to 0.60 A. A steeper line would mean a smaller resistance.
alt: Graph of current against voltage: a straight line through the origin through (4.5 V, 0.3 A) and (9 V, 0.60 A).
description: The horizontal axis is the voltage in volts; the vertical axis is the current in amperes.
The measured point (4.5 V, 0.3 A) gives R = 4.5/0.3 = 15 Ω.
The line is I = V/15: through the origin, so I ∝ V (Ohm's law). At 9 V, I = 9/15 = 0.60 A.
